title: Concordance Altar
pages: Craft this ninth t6 controller from the Reliquary Core produced by the Reliquary Stand, four bookshelves, two copper blocks and two amethyst shards. The core is the mandatory progression gate.

Place an enchanting table immediately below and an amethyst cluster above; place bookshelves two blocks north and south and copper blocks directly east and west. Keep the north and south controller faces clear for item ports. All six parts must remain loaded and intact. Breaking one stops processing immediately. Optional stabilisers: amethyst blocks on the four diagonal corners at altar height each add 1 stability (base 1); an Astral Font holding at least 100 lumen in a corner adds 2 instead (maximum 9). Neither is required for forming.

Hold a full base batch in the main hand and the reagent in the offhand, then right-click. Thirty dye concordances tint four white candles or four white banners with one dye, saving dye in large decorative builds. Two Reliquary Cores and four amethyst shards fuse into a Concordance Seal for the final t5 controller. Quenched Obsidian fuses a water bucket with two blaze powder into two obsidian and returns the bucket; its fire and water oppose, so it needs two amethyst blocks on the altar's diagonal corners (see Material Traits).

Rites of reconciliation and unreality need more stability than amethyst alone can give; JEI shows each rite's required stability, and a rite never asks less than its inputs' trait instability. Crying obsidian with a sea lantern reconciles fire and water, light and dark into three ochre froglights (stability 4). A sealed steel plate with two phantom membranes yields a shulker shell (5). A calibrated sculk sensor with four ender pearls condenses an echo shard (6), and four amethyst blocks quickened by an echo shard become budding amethyst (9, all four corners holding charged Astral Fonts). The last two carry calm traits but make what nature does not renew, so their unreality sets the floor. Each font the rite leans on pays 100 lumen.

Manual use: hold a full base batch in the main hand and the reagent in the offhand. Automation: feed base stock into slot 0 and the reagent into slot 1 through the north face; take products from the south face after sneak-using it with both hands empty to switch it to output (the bottom face is the enchanting table). Hand-held rites resolve immediately: insufficient stability backlashes, consuming the reagent and hurting the user while leaving the base intact. Hopper-fed rites take 40 ticks. Hoppers and item pipes can use these faces; sneak-use with empty hands cycles a face between input, output and disabled, and plain empty-hand use collects output. An automated rite whose stability is short pauses with nothing spent instead of backlashing, so add stabilisers or recharge the corner fonts; it pays font lumen like a manual rite. Containers such as the water bucket's bucket go to a second output slot. There is no fluid or FE port. JEI lists every loaded paired recipe; ambiguous matches resolve by recipe ID. If no recipe matches the held items, or only one hand holds an item, the altar runs a trait assay instead and consumes nothing. A recipe whose product would hold a trait its inputs lack is refused (see Material Traits); automation holds such a batch.
